questions.q: Arrange the free radicals in decreasing stability: CH₃•, (CH₃)₃C•, CH₂=CH•, CH₂=CHCH₂•.
questions.explain: Allyl is resonance stabilised (C–H BDE 89 kcal/mol), tert-butyl gains from hyperconjugation (96.5), while the vinyl radical (111) is less stable even than methyl (105).

questions.q: The hybridisation of carbon in the methyl free radical and in the methyl carbanion is, respectively:
questions.explain: •CH₃ is planar with the odd electron in a pure p orbital, so it is sp²; CH₃⁻ is pyramidal, sp³.

questions.q: Which statement about carbocation stability is correct according to hydride ion affinity data?
options: The cyclopropylmethyl cation is more stable than the cyclopropenyl cation
The methyl cation is more stable than the vinyl cation
The phenyl cation is more stable than the ethyl cation
The tropylium cation is more stable than the tert-butyl cation
questions.explain: Aromatic tropylium has the lowest HIA (201 against 231 kcal/mol for tert-butyl). Cyclopropenyl (221) beats cyclopropylmethyl (249), vinyl (287) beats methyl (312), and phenyl (298) is less stable than ethyl (273).

questions.q: Arrange in decreasing stability: C₆H₅C≡C⁻, (C₆H₅)₃C⁻, C₆H₅CH₂⁻, CH₃⁻.
questions.explain: Rank carbanions by parent pKa in DMSO: phenylacetylene 28.8, triphenylmethane 30.6, toluene about 43, methane about 56. The sp carbanion edges out even the triply benzylic one, which is the trap.
